review.readiness_note: Visual sign-off for the captured 390px viewport. The document-end tab bar is an accepted capture arrangement. Click destinations, Request menu behavior, permissions and query-failure handling still require runtime verification; the capture does not establish those behaviors.
review.why: The production screen preserves Frame Shift’s source-to-decision relationship rather than merely copying its colors. Work begins on the left, identity starts 12px lower on the right, and source captions lead into distinct inspection and request actions. Cars use complete photographs followed by stepped, unboxed monthly terms. The mineral surface, restrained cobalt, strong hierarchy and literal status text match the approved language. The header, city control, captions, prices and navigation fit without visible clipping or collisions. Cars appear farther down because the explicitly approved phone layout presents people vertically; that is not desktop-composition drift. No release-blocking visual or exposed-functionality regression is evident.
review.verdict: Frame Shift was faithfully transferred to this 390px production screen, with real data and visible functionality preserved; approve this viewport.
